_comment: Model bank for scripts/gen_random_workload.py, platform spike.
Three models have spike profile data on both the RVV and scalar lanes:
mlp_control (fp32), dronet (int8) and yolov8_nano (int8). Dispatch graphs
are the .fp32-tagged ones emit_dispatch_graph.py writes -- the profile
CSVs are always tagged .fp32 regardless of the real quant, so the
scheduler's basename match needs that spelling (see
Period and window ranges bracket the values the hand-written spike
workloads use: mlp_control at 10 ms, dronet at 20-1000 ms, yolov8_nano
non-periodic because its 629 ms chain does not fit any control cadence.

mlp_control.variant_note: Drone control policy, 7 dispatches, ~0.39 ms per instance on the scalar lane. fp32 only: this model has no int8 variant.

dronet.variant_note: Vision steering net, 24 dispatches, ~28.4 ms per instance on RVV and ~454 ms on scalar -- a 16x lane gap, which is what makes the periodic lane choice matter on this target.

yolov8_nano.variant_note: Object detection, 212 dispatches, ~628.9 ms on RVV and ~10438 ms on scalar. Non-periodic: its chain is longer than any control cadence here, so it defines the makespan.
